chunks: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from al-Hasan, from some of his companions, from Misma', from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: Verily, he صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade a man from urinating in flowing water except in a case of necessity, and he said: Indeed, water has inhabitants. So the correct understanding in this matter is that we carry it upon a type of karahah (disapproval), not upon prohibition and obligation.

key_terms.الْإِيجَابِ: obligation, also negated as the intended legal force here
key_terms.الْحَظْرِ: prohibition, which the text explicitly negates as the intended meaning
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: disapproval, the legal sense intended here rather than strict prohibition
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْجَارِي: flowing water, the specific type of water mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.ضَرُورَةٍ: necessity, an exceptional circumstance permitting the act
key_terms.نَهَى: forbade, indicating a discouraging or prohibitive command depending on context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on urinating in flowing water in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade urinating in flowing water except out of necessity. The text then clarifies that this prohibition is to be understood as karahah (disapproval) rather than strict tahrim (prohibition), indicating an etiquette and legal ruling related to ritual purity and conduct.
